chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

Regarding the wealth of the orphan, is there Zakat upon it? He said: When it is a deposit, there is no Zakat upon it, and when you work with it, you are responsible (guarantor) for it, and the profit is for the orphan.
ai.seo_question: Is Zakat due on an orphan's wealth if it is kept as a deposit versus being invested?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a critical distinction in Shia jurisprudence between passive custody and active management of an orphan's wealth. It clarifies that Zakat liability is tied to the wealth's productive status, while the guardian assumes full liability (daman) for the principal if they engage in trade, ensuring that all commercial gains accrue exclusively to the orphan.
